Palmetto non-profits with highest government grant revenue in 2024
N. L. Sawyer
Renaissance Arts and Education Inc. led non-profits in Palmetto, Florida in reported government grant revenue in 2024, with $2,941,655 in government grants reported in its IRS Form 990 filing and $33,332,293 in total revenue. Government grants made up 8.8% of its reported total revenue.
The ranking reflects non-profits with available Form 990-series government grant revenue data that met the ranking's data criteria and may not include every non-profit in the city.
The ranking is based on IRS Form 990 filings, the annual information returns most tax-exempt organizations file with the IRS. The form includes reported revenue, expenses, assets, governance information and compensation paid to certain people, making it a public source for comparing large tax-exempt organizations' finances.
The figures reflect what each organization reported for its filing year, including total revenue, contributions, government grants, compensation, the number of employees and assets at the start and end of the year. Because nonprofits can differ by mission, structure and accounting period, the totals are best read as reported financial measures, not as a direct measure of local charitable activity.
Among the 6 ranked organizations with calculable government-grant shares, the median government-grant share was 32.6% of reported total revenue. From Cradle To College Foundation reported the highest share of revenue from government grants at 99.1%.
In 2024, From Cradle To College Foundation received $325,000 in government grant revenue, up from $275,000 the prior year, an increase of $50,000 or 18.2%.
Renaissance Arts and Education Inc. reported total contributions of $2,941,655. Gulf Shellfish Institute Inc reported $503,121 in total contributions, with $28,250 categorized as all other contributions. Feeding Empty Little Tummies Inc. reported $567,278 in total contributions, including $454,778 categorized as all other contributions and $92,385 reported as non-cash. Genesis Health Services Inc reported $152,370 in total contributions, of which $67,000 was categorized as all other contributions.
Renaissance Arts and Education Inc. saw its asset balances rise from $46,288,717 at the beginning of the year to $50,662,628 by year-end, a 9.4% increase. Gulf Shellfish Institute Inc reported asset balances increasing from $29,764 to $69,446, a 133.3% increase. From Cradle To College Foundation reported assets of $190,067 at the start of the year and $194,913 at year-end, a change of 2.5%. North River Care Inc saw assets fall from $534,183 to $516,782, a change of -3.3%. Feeding Empty Little Tummies Inc. increased its assets from $710,220 to $924,664, a 30.2% increase. Genesis Health Services Inc grew its asset balance from $591,964 at the start of the year to $847,728 at year-end, a 43.2% increase.
Tax-exempt organizations include a wide range of groups, such as charities, foundations, educational institutions and other mission-driven organizations. Under IRS rules, 501(c)(3) organizations must be organized and operated for exempt purposes, and their earnings cannot benefit private shareholders or individuals.
